Three properties limit what the oracle measures. It is fault-triggered: it
predicts only when a fault arrives, one page per fault. It runs at most $L$ ranks
ahead of demand, and we report only $L = 4096$. And with the prefetcher on, few
faults arrive, so it issues few predictions: about 2{,}200 work items per
Stencil-24K run. Our speculation results therefore measure one fault-triggered
staging design with near-perfect knowledge of the future; they are not an upper
bound on off-path staging in general.

If speculation's benefit runs through the density threshold, the threshold can
be moved directly. Lowering it from the shipped 51 to 0, with no speculation,
makes the stock driver 9.57\% faster on the same stencil workload (confirmatory
test), and the oracle-driven speculation configuration at the shipped threshold
is 6.4\% slower than it. At matched thresholds, speculation adds at most 2.8\%,
and nothing detectable at threshold 0 or 10 (minimum detectable effects 2.0\%
and 2.3\% at the family's corrected level).
new:
If speculation's benefit runs through the density threshold, the threshold can
be moved directly. At matched thresholds, speculation adds at most 2.8\%, and
nothing detectable at threshold 0 or 10 (minimum detectable effects 2.0\% and
2.3\% at the family's corrected level). Lowering the threshold from the shipped
51 to 0, with no speculation, makes the stock driver 9.57\% faster on the same
stencil workload (confirmatory test). Part of that gain is not on the GPU fault
path: the same threshold governs prefetching for CPU faults, and at threshold 0
the host faults six times less often while initialising the array, a saving
GPU-side staging cannot obtain.

old:
If staging gains only by helping regions pass the threshold, lowering the
threshold should gain at least as much without staging. E6 tested this with a
second pre-registered trigger: it would fire if any stock configuration at a
lower threshold was not significantly slower than C7-W512 at 51. It fired. C0 at
threshold 0 is faster than C7-W512 at 51, which is 6.39\% slower than it; at
threshold 10 the oracle is 4.72\% slower, and at 25 the two do not differ
detectably (\texttt{E6.F1.C7W512-t51\_vs\_C0-t0}, \texttt{-t10}, \texttt{-t25}).

At matched thresholds, speculation adds little. Its gain is $-0.85\%$ at
threshold 0 and $-0.28\%$ at 10, neither significant, against minimum detectable
effects of 2.04\% and 2.28\% at the family's level, and 2.76\% at 25, which is
significant (\texttt{E6.wall.C7W512-t0\_vs\_C0-t0}, \texttt{-t10}, \texttt{-t25},
\texttt{E6.mde\_family.stencil\_wall}). Staging still removes faults at every
threshold, 5.3\% of them at 0 and 22.1\% at 25 (\texttt{E6.demand.*}), but at low
thresholds the prefetcher has already taken most regions, and the faults that
remain are too few to matter: one pre-registered expectation predicted a
wall-clock gain from the 5.3\% at threshold 0, and it failed (X4).
new:
If staging gains only by helping regions pass the threshold, it should add
little once the threshold is already low. E6 tested this directly, by comparing
speculation with no speculation at the same threshold. Speculation adds little.
Its gain is $-0.85\%$ at threshold 0 and $-0.28\%$ at 10, neither significant,
against minimum detectable effects of 2.04\% and 2.28\% at the family's level,
and 2.76\% at 25, which is significant (\texttt{E6.wall.C7W512-t0\_vs\_C0-t0},
\texttt{-t10}, \texttt{-t25}, \texttt{E6.mde\_family.stencil\_wall}). Staging
still removes faults at every threshold, 5.3\% of them at 0 and 22.1\% at 25
(\texttt{E6.demand.*}), but at low thresholds the prefetcher has already taken
most regions, and the faults that remain are too few to matter: one
pre-registered expectation predicted a wall-clock gain from the 5.3\% at
threshold 0, and it failed (X4).

E6 also compared speculation at the shipped threshold with the stock driver at
lower thresholds. A second pre-registered trigger would fire if any stock
configuration at a lower threshold was not significantly slower than C7-W512 at
51. It fired. C0 at threshold 0 is faster than C7-W512 at 51, which is 6.39\%
slower than it; at threshold 10 the oracle is 4.72\% slower, and at 25 the two do
not differ detectably (\texttt{E6.F1.C7W512-t51\_vs\_C0-t0}, \texttt{-t10},
\texttt{-t25}). This comparison is less clean than the matched one: part of the
gain from a lower threshold comes from fewer CPU faults during initialisation
(Section~\ref{sec:thr-dense}), which GPU-side staging cannot obtain.
